name: headline
description: The UIDS headline (`.headline`, plus its legacy `.bold-headline` alias) — heading-level text with optional highlight, underline, uppercase and serif treatments. Renders as `<component :is="level">` around a slot with no internal markup of its own; consumers author the `.headline__heading`/`.headline__text` inner span themselves (see behavior).

figma.note: Set 168:75, 60 variants (Level x Style x Alignment), page Components / Headline. Style collapses text_style + underline + highlight (Button precedent); combos beyond the five axis values are code-only. Alignment (Default/Center) was added 2026-08-24 with the alignment option. On-gold flips and negative are context frames, not axes; center IS an axis as of that change.
axisRationale: CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (found while building the banner set, fixed with the design system owner's approval): the Serif variants at H2-H6 drew Zilla Slab MEDIUM, where _headline-mixins.scss:38-41 declares `font-weight: $font-weight-bold` and a live H2 measures 700 at a 1020 viewport. H1/Serif was already correct, which is what made the other five look deliberate. All six are now Bold. Fonts are not captured by figma-readback.js, so this correction does not move the snapshot.

options.name: level
options.description: Heading level — selects the rendered tag via Vue's dynamic <component :is>.

figma.notes: h5/h6 additionally get a shorter underline bar (5px/4px vs 6px) when underline is on — geometry, not a separate axis value; see geometryNotTokenized.

options.name: text_style
options.description: Type treatment. '' (the real Vue default) renders the base treatment with no extra class; serif switches to the Zilla Slab stack + bold weight (both already token-driven via the typography primitives — $font-family-serif/$font-weight-bold compile to var(--uiowa-font-*) chains, deliberately NOT duplicated in this contract's tokensUsed); uppercase switches to Antonio + uppercase + bold.

code.notes: The Vue prop's real default is the empty string '' (no validator constrains it to an enum) — Storybook's own control labels it 'default'. Kept as '' here rather than a friendly 'default' string so the contract's default field text-matches the Vue source exactly (check-contracts compares them literally).

figma.notes: Shares the Style axis with underline and highlight (Brand Bar/Button precedent: collapsing related booleans into one visible axis) — Level × Style = 6 × 5 = 30 variants. Combinations beyond the five axis values (e.g. serif+underline, uppercase+highlight) are code-only: use the code props for that combination, same as Button's transparent+light_font.

options.name: underline
options.description: Adds a gold underline bar below the headline (gray on a gold/brain-reversed background). h5/h6 get a shorter bar — see geometryNotTokenized.

figma.notes: Shares the Style axis with text_style and highlight — see text_style's notes.

options.name: highlight
options.description: Wraps an inner <span> in a gold background block (black on gold/brain-reversed backgrounds). Renders nothing unless the slot content actually contains a <span> — see behavior.

figma.notes: Shares the Style axis with text_style and underline — see text_style's notes.

options.name: alignment
options.description: Horizontal alignment of the heading text AND of the underline bar. '' (the Vue default) emits no class and is the INHERIT case — the heading takes whatever text-align its container supplies. 'center' emits the already-shipped `.headline--center`, which does two separate things that only look like one: `text-align: center` on the heading (_headline.scss:23) centers the text, and `margin-right/left: auto` on the underline bar (_headline-mixins.scss:96) centers the bar. The second is why this is an option rather than inherited context — see code.notes.

code.notes: A container's `text-align: center` centers the TEXT but NOT the underline bar: the bar is a `:after` with `display: block; width: 75px` and default zero side margins, so text-align (which positions inline content) cannot move it — verified in the compiled `dist/uids.css`, where `margin-right/left: auto` on a headline `:after` occurs ONLY in selectors gated on `.headline--center`. So the class must land on the heading itself, and only a prop can put it there. There is deliberately no 'left' or 'right' value: neither has a shipped class, and '' already covers the left case in a left-aligned container — adding them would be new CSS invented for the contract rather than exposed by it. Unlike text_style (no validator, documented as-shipped), this prop DOES declare a validator: it is new code, and the as-shipped-don't-fix rule protects 4.x behaviour, not new additions.

figma.notes: A full second axis (Level x Style x Alignment = 60 variants), NOT a sixth Style value. Alignment is orthogonal to style, and the evidence is in the repo: both real `.headline--center` usages combine it with serif AND underline (src/components/callout/Callout.stories.js:53, src/components/inline/Inline.stories.js:168), a combination a collapsed Style value could not express — where serif+underline itself legitimately collapses because those are competing treatments of the same text. In Figma the Center variants are 480px fixed-width (the Default variants hug their text, where centering would be invisible) and carry counterAxisAlignItems=CENTER, which is the direct analogue of the bar's margin-inline auto.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The headline's rendered content. Headline.vue wraps only <component :is="level"> around this slot — no internal markup of its own.
slots.behavior: Consumers author `.headline__heading`/`.headline__text` (and Stat's `.headline__prefix`/`.headline__suffix`) themselves; Headline.vue does not add them. See the required inner-markup protocol in `behavior`: highlight and highlight-word styling target descendant `span` elements, so slot content must include an actual `<span>` for those rules to render anything.

figma.notes: Modelled as a text layer bound to the headline instance. The highlight/underline/uppercase treatments are baked into the Style axis's variant artwork rather than represented as separate nested layers.

geometryNotTokenized.highlight-word-padding: 0.85rem 1rem base (headline-highlight-word mixin, span, mixins:54); .2rem 1rem 0.5rem 1rem for the serif+highlight combo (`.headline--highlight.headline--serif span`, _headline.scss:42-46); .4rem 1.2rem .8rem for the uppercase highlight-word variant AND the uppercase+highlight combo (headline-highlight-word-uppercase mixins:70; `.headline--highlight.headline--uppercase span` _headline.scss:98-103 — same value in both places), plus margin-top/margin-bottom .8rem on the uppercase variant (mixins:68-69).
geometryNotTokenized.highlight-block-spacing: margin-bottom: 8px, padding: 2px 0 on the highlight block itself (headline-highlight mixin, mixins:46-47) — one-off geometry alongside the tokenized line-height:1.7.
geometryNotTokenized.underline-bar: 75px wide x 6px tall bar, margin-top: 15px (headline-underline mixin, mixins:90-92); h5 overrides height to 5px (_headline.scss:78), h6 to 4px (_headline.scss:88).
geometryNotTokenized.underline-padding-bottom: padding-bottom: $sm = 0.625rem (headline-underline mixin, mixins:84). $sm already exists as the space.62 primitive (consumed by button/icon-gap), but repointing this Sass var to var(--uiowa-space-62) is the deferred cross-component $xsm...$xxxlg sweep (tokens/README) — left as raw $sm here, not part of this contract's tokensUsed.
geometryNotTokenized.box-decoration-break: box-decoration-break: clone / -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone (headline-highlight-word mixin, mixins:55-56) — a line-wrap rendering mechanic, not a design value.
geometryNotTokenized.negative-and-center: SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-24: `.headline--center` is no longer class-only — it is the `alignment` option's 'center' value (see options, changes[0]), and Figma models it as the Alignment axis, not a context frame. What remains true is the geometry: `text-align: center` plus `margin-right/left: auto` on the underline `:after`. The pre-option center appliers were story markup only (src/components/callout/Callout.stories.js:53, src/components/inline/Inline.stories.js:168) — the Callout citation read `:51` here until 2026-08-24 and is actually `:53`. `.headline--negative`: negative-is-class-only.
geometryNotTokenized.negative-is-class-only: `.headline--negative` (white text + links, headline-negative mixin) IS still class-only, exposed by no Vue prop — Button's caps-and-lowercase precedent: documented here, NOT modeled as an option; exposing it is a public-shape decision still deferred. negative has ZERO source-level appliers in either repo (only the SCSS definitions — reachable via editor-entered classes at most; see knownIssues) and appears on the Figma page as a context frame, not an axis. Its color IS tokenized (headline/negative/color) since the SCSS rule ships live.

behavior: Required inner-markup protocol: Headline.vue renders only `<component :is="level">` around its default slot — it adds no `.headline__heading`/`.headline__text` markup. Consumers supply it (Banner.vue renders `<span class="headline__heading" v-html="...">`; Stat.vue renders `.headline__prefix`/`.headline__suffix`; SiteNow's headline.html.twig the same `.headline__heading` span). `.headline--highlight`'s highlight-word styling (headline-highlight-word mixin) and the uppercase variant both target descendant `span` elements — content with no inner `<span>` gets the `highlight`/`underline`/`uppercase` boolean classes with no visible highlight-word background. The stale @todo in Headline.stories.js:114 (`HighlightedSingleWord`, 'Figure out how to get this example working') is a symptom of this protocol not being obvious at the story layer. One selector escapes the prop entirely: behavior[3].

`[class*="bg-"]` ancestor context forces `a { color: inherit }` (_headline.scss:11-15) — note the single-hyphen `bg-` attribute-contains matcher catches both `bg--*` (solid backgrounds) and `bg-pattern--*` (pattern backgrounds).

On-gold flips: inside a `[class*="bg--gold"]` ancestor, highlight colors invert (background flips gold→black via headline.highlight.background-on-gold, text flips black→white via headline.highlight.color-on-gold — mixins:59-62,72-76), the uppercase font-weight drops from 700 to a declared 400 (headline.uppercase.font-weight-on-gold — _headline.scss:57-59, mixins:75; Antonio ships no 400 face, so it renders the static 300), and the underline bar switches from gold to gray/100 (headline.underline.color-on-gold — mixins:103-107). A further nested `[class*="bg--gold"] [class*="bg--black"]` context flips the highlight colors back to the DEFAULT (gold background / black text — mixins:77-80), reusing headline.highlight.background/color rather than a third token pair.

THE UPPERCASE HIGHLIGHT-WORD SELECTORS ESCAPE THE `highlight` PROP: `.headline--uppercase .headline__heading span` and `.headline--uppercase .headline__text span` (_headline.scss:62-66) do NOT include `.headline--highlight` at all, so any span inside an uppercase headline's `.headline__heading`/`.headline__text` gets the highlight-word treatment REGARDLESS of the prop. That unconditional path is how uppercase hero headlines highlight words; the non-uppercase `.headline--highlight span` path (_headline.scss:48-52) is the only one gated on the prop's class. Read with behavior[0]'s markup protocol.
changes: 2026-08-24 — HEADLINE GAINS AN `alignment` OPTION, AND THE COMPONENT SET REOPENS TO DO IT. The design system owner ruled this contract-first out of a generated-page review: a centred section wants a centred heading, and there was no way to ask for one. This is a PUBLIC-SHAPE ADDITION, so unlike cta.json changes[0] the version moves (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, badge/logo precedent). (1) It reopens a set recorded as CLOSED after banner and card — the closure is about not MIGRATING new components, and Headline was already migrated; this adds an option to an existing contract, which the contract-first rule explicitly contemplates. Two more things about it are deliberate and should not be "tidied" later: changes[1].

2026-08-24, continues changes[0]. (2) IT ADDS NO SCSS. `.headline--center` has shipped since before the migration (_headline.scss:23 plus the bar's margin-inline auto at _headline-mixins.scss:96); it was documented in geometryNotTokenized as class-only, and all this change does is put a prop in front of it. So no pixel moves anywhere, and the option is 'exposed', not 'invented' — the distinction the no-planned-options rule cares about. No `.bold-headline--center` alias exists and none was added: the legacy alias doubling is as-shipped debt (see knownIssues), not a pattern to extend. Why the values are '' and 'center' ONLY: changes[2].

2026-08-24, continues changes[0]. (3) THE VALUES ARE '' AND 'center' ONLY. 'left'/'right' were considered and DECLINED for the reason badge's size modifier was declined on 2026-08-21 — one honest answer beats a first instalment: neither has a shipped class, '' already covers left-in-a-left-container, and the rule this option exists to serve (heading-alignment-follows-content) actively discourages forcing a heading against its container's grain. Recorded here so the absence reads as settled rather than half-finished.

2026-09-01. The GUIDANCE on `underline` reversed; the option itself is unchanged. contracts/rules.json underline-scope previously restricted the gold bar to the first heading of a content or text area and named card grids and parallel tile sets as cases to avoid — so a page built to the rule underlined one heading and left the rest plain. Reviewed against a generated landing page, the design system owner ruled the other way: a site chooses one heading treatment and applies it to every section heading, making the bar a per-site style rather than a scarce emphasis marker. Recorded here because nothing about Headline's shape moved and a later reader comparing pages built before and after this date would otherwise read the difference as drift. The surviving restriction is that a sub-heading inside a section is never underlined.
knownIssues: `.bold-headline--*` is a legacy alias that DOUBLES every selector in this file and is LIVE downstream (both uids_base hero twigs render `bold-headline--serif bold-headline`, and cta_uids3.scss's `.bold-headline`/`.headline` rule pair) — it cannot be removed in 4.x despite the file's own `// @todo Remove .bold-headline variations.` at _headline.scss:5. Dedupe in 5.x.

Headline.stories.js's Default.args includes stale args (`size: 'large'`, plus argTypes for `url`, `aria_describedby`, `class`) that do not correspond to any real Headline.vue prop — `size` is inert, and `url`/`aria_describedby`/`class` are not declared in defineProps at all. Only `level`, `text_style`, `underline`, `highlight` are real.

Highlight+uppercase+serif triple combos have distinct, hand-tuned span paddings rather than a composable rule: base highlight 0.85rem 1rem; +serif .2rem 1rem 0.5rem 1rem; +uppercase .4rem 1.2rem .8rem (see geometryNotTokenized).

The `HighlightedSingleWord` story (Headline.stories.js:114-122) carries an unresolved `// @todo Figure out how to get this example working` — see the inner-markup protocol note in `behavior` for the likely mechanism.

`.bold-headline--caps .headline__headline span` (_headline.scss:48) references a class `.headline__headline` that appears nowhere else in the codebase (verified by repo-wide grep) — almost certainly a typo for `.headline__heading`. Low-severity: it's one of three comma-separated selectors sharing the same mixin, and the other two (`.bold-headline--highlight span`, `.headline--highlight span`) still match, so the visual isn't broken by it — but it's dead as written. Flag for a 5.x cleanup alongside the .bold-headline dedupe.

Headline.vue:4 declares `const name = 'uids-headine'` (missing the 'l' in 'headline') and never reads it — dead code, same pattern as the (also unused) `const name = 'uids-button'` already documented in the Button contract. The component's actual registered tag is `uids-headline` (see Card.vue, Cta.vue, Banner.vue usage), not this typo'd local constant.

`.headline--negative` has zero source-level appliers in both repos (verified: no twig/theme/php/vue/js/stories usage — only the SCSS definitions and compiled bundles) — a candidate for the same 5.x public-shape review as Button's dead .bttn--link value. The SCSS rule and headline/negative/color stay, tokenized as-shipped.

STILL OPEN: H2/Serif sits at 28px where every other H2 variant is 31.2 — the only level whose serif size differs from its siblings — and heading-serif-h2 vs heading-h2 should share the ramp (h1 is byte-identical between them). Not changed yet because it needs the serif ramp measured against the Semantic size variables' small(600) mode first. Moved here from identity.figma.note on 2026-08-21: an open defect belongs in knownIssues, where a reader looks for defects.

a11y.notes: level is presentational-structural: it selects the rendered hN tag, so consumers own document-outline correctness (nothing prevents an h1 rendered inside an h4 context; one-h1-per-page per rules.json). text-transform: uppercase (text_style=uppercase) can alter some screen readers' pronunciation of acronyms — authors should write natural case and let CSS transform. Highlight/underline are purely visual (background + pseudo-element) with no ARIA surface; the required inner-span protocol (see behavior) is presentation-only markup.
